Command: Pay for damage caused by an ox goring another ox
Summary: If one man's ox gores another man's ox so that it dies, the living ox is sold and the price divided, and the dead ox divided as well; if the ox was known to gore, the owner pays ox for ox.
Commandment: Pay for damage caused by an ox goring another ox, as the Law scales it to the owner's knowledge.
Application: Even animal against animal has its measure: shared loss where no fault was known, full repayment where danger was known and ignored. The distinction between accident and culpable negligence runs through the whole law of damages.
Purpose: To make wrongs right: damage between neighbours' animals is shared or repaid according to what the owner knew.
